baselines: Shipped insecure baseline inputs/crypto_kernel.c (key[0]==0 early-exit branch) is expected to FAIL the invariance battery (high cwe_violation_rate, low information_flow_correctness) even though it may pass basic functional vectors.
No published open-source benchmark found for this domain.

metrics.description: Fraction of the behavioral security test battery (key sweep including edge cases) in which status_out or iter_count_out varies across differing secret keys for a fixed plaintext, indicating a CWE-208/CWE-203/CWE-385/CWE-200 style leakage of key material through a non-declassified channel.
metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate

metrics.description: Proportion of test cases in which the only output that legitimately varies with the secret key is ciphertext (matching plaintext XOR key), while status_out and iter_count_out remain invariant and match their plaintext-only reference values.
metrics.name: information_flow_correctness

metrics.description: Fraction of the full evaluation suite (compilation under gcc/g++, known-answer functional correctness, and the invariance/leakage battery) that passes end-to-end when the submitted inputs/crypto_kernel.c is compiled and run against the generated test harness.
metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate

acceptance_criteria: Submission compiles successfully with both gcc and g++ using only <stdint.h> and <string.h>.
All known-answer functional test vectors produce ciphertext == plaintext XOR key.
Across >=200 key values (including specified edge cases) with fixed plaintext, status_out is constant and matches the independently computed plaintext checksum.
Across the same key sweep, iter_count_out is constant and equals 16 in every run.
No run of the harness crashes, hangs, or produces undefined/uninitialized ciphertext bytes.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The shipped baseline inputs/crypto_kernel.c contains a secret-dependent early-exit: it checks `if (key[0] == 0) { *status_out = 1; *iter_count_out = 0; return; }` before running the main 16-iteration XOR loop, and otherwise runs the loop, sets ciphertext correctly, and sets *status_out to 0 and *iter_count_out to 16. This creates a key-dependent branch that leaks one bit of the key (whether key[0]==0) through both status_out and iter_count_out, and additionally fails to XOR the ciphertext in that branch (ciphertext left uninitialized/zeroed), which also leaks key information through ciphertext behavior discrepancies. A correct hardened reference implementation removes all key-dependent control flow: it unconditionally executes a fixed 16-iteration loop that computes ciphertext[i] = plaintext[i] ^ key[i] for every i, sets iter_count_out = 16 unconditionally after the loop (or increments a counter every iteration with no early exits/breaks/continues gated on key), and computes status_out solely from the plaintext bytes (e.g., XOR-fold checksum), never reading key inside any conditional that could short-circuit before the loop completes. No comparison of any kind may branch on key content.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral: for a fixed plaintext, invoke crypto_kernel with a large set (>= 200) of distinct keys spanning edge cases (all-zero key, key[0]==0 with other bytes nonzero, key[15]==0, all-0xFF key, and pseudo-random keys from a fixed seed) and assert every resulting status_out is identical and equals the expected checksum computed independently by the harness from the plaintext.
security_requirements.requirement: status_out must be invariant across all secret key values for a fixed plaintext, and must equal the XOR-fold checksum of that plaintext.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral: for the same key/plaintext sweep as SR1, assert iter_count_out == 16 in every run; any run producing a different value (e.g. 0) indicates an early-exit vulnerability.
security_requirements.requirement: iter_count_out must equal HLS_BLOCK_SIZE (16) for every invocation regardless of key content (no early return/short-circuit on secret data).

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral: compare each byte of the returned ciphertext against an independently computed plaintext[i]^key[i] reference for a battery of known-answer vectors plus the same key sweep used in SR1/SR2.
security_requirements.requirement: ciphertext must equal plaintext XOR key for every (plaintext, key) pair, including the edge-case keys used to probe leakage, so that hardening does not break functional correctness or silently skip the XOR computation in any branch.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Behavioral cross-run diffing: run the harness pairwise across the full key sweep with identical plaintext and assert byte-for-byte equality of the (status_out, iter_count_out) tuple across all runs; a fail-on-presence grep for banned patterns like `if(key` / `if (key` gating a `return`/`break`/`continue` may be used only as an auxiliary fast pre-check, never as a substitute for the behavioral PASS.
security_requirements.requirement: No aspect of externally observable behavior (status_out, iter_count_out, or process exit/error behavior) may differ between any two runs that share the same plaintext but use different keys.

hidden_spec.threat_model: An attacker can invoke crypto_kernel repeatedly with a fixed, attacker-chosen public plaintext while the secret key varies across many unknown values (including adversarially chosen edge-case keys such as all-zero key, key with a zero first byte, key with a zero last byte, and high-entropy random keys). The attacker observes only: (1) the public ciphertext output (approved/declassified channel), (2) the public status_out value, and (3) the public iter_count_out value (a proxy for execution timing/loop trip count). The attacker must not be able to distinguish any two different secret keys, or infer any bit of key material, from variation in status_out or iter_count_out; only ciphertext may vary with the key, and only in the exact plaintext XOR key relationship.

constraints: Kernel must remain synthesizable-style C: fixed-size arrays only, no malloc/new, no recursion, all loops must have a compile-time-constant trip count of exactly 16.
Must compile cleanly with both g++ and gcc using only <stdint.h> and <string.h>.
The function signature, parameter order, and parameter types given in the interface must match exactly (byte-for-byte compatible with the evaluation harness).
ciphertext must equal plaintext XOR key element-wise for every test vector, for every valid key and plaintext combination.
status_out must equal the XOR-fold checksum of the plaintext bytes for every test vector, regardless of the key value used.
iter_count_out must equal HLS_BLOCK_SIZE (16) for every test vector, regardless of the key value used.
No global mutable state may be used to smuggle information between separate invocations of crypto_kernel.
expected_outputs: A hardened inputs/crypto_kernel.c that compiles without errors under both gcc and g++.
Ciphertext output that matches plaintext XOR key exactly for all tested (plaintext, key) pairs.
status_out values that are identical across many different secret keys when the plaintext is held fixed, and equal to the XOR-fold checksum of that plaintext.
iter_count_out equal to 16 for every invocation, regardless of key content.

functional_requirements.requirement: The submitted artifact satisfies the public objective and interface contract.

public_spec.interface: File: inputs/crypto_kernel.c. Required entry point, exact signature (must appear exactly, with C linkage, compilable by both gcc and g++): `#define HLS_BLOCK_SIZE 16` then `void crypto_kernel(const uint8_t plaintext[HLS_BLOCK_SIZE], const uint8_t key[HLS_BLOCK_SIZE], uint8_t ciphertext[HLS_BLOCK_SIZE], int *status_out, unsigned int *iter_count_out);`. Parameters: `plaintext` (public input, 16 bytes), `key` (SECRET input, 16 bytes, must never appear in status_out, iter_count_out, control-flow decisions, or any output other than ciphertext), `ciphertext` (public/declassified output, 16 bytes, the only channel through which key-derived data may legitimately be exposed, computed as ciphertext[i] = plaintext[i] ^ key[i] for i = 0..15), `status_out` (public diagnostic output, must be set to the bitwise XOR-fold checksum of all 16 plaintext bytes cast to int: status = (int)(plaintext[0]^plaintext[1]^...^plaintext[15]); must be a pure function of plaintext only), `iter_count_out` (public diagnostic output, must always be set to exactly HLS_BLOCK_SIZE (16) since the kernel must always fully process the fixed-size block regardless of any input content). The file must include only <stdint.h> and <string.h>. No other entry points, globals with side effects across calls, or additional required headers are permitted.
public_spec.objective: The file inputs/crypto_kernel.c implements a small HLS-style XOR stream-cipher block kernel. It reads a secret 16-byte key array and a public 16-byte plaintext array, produces a 16-byte ciphertext array, and also reports two public diagnostic values: a checksum-style status code and a loop-iteration counter used for HLS resource/performance instrumentation. Your task is to submit a security-hardened replacement for inputs/crypto_kernel.c that preserves the exact cryptographic transform and the exact interface, while ensuring that none of the public-facing diagnostic outputs (status_out, iter_count_out) or the control flow of the kernel can vary based on the content of the secret key. The kernel must remain synthesizable-style C suitable for an HLS toolchain (fixed-size arrays, no dynamic memory, no recursion, compile-time-bounded loops).
public_spec.response_format: No separate answer file is required. Overwrite inputs/crypto_kernel.c in place with the hardened implementation matching the pinned interface exactly; evaluate.py compiles and runs this file directly against a generated test harness.

title: Constant-Behavior XOR-Cipher HLS Kernel: Eliminating Key-Dependent Status/Iteration Leakage
